literal: Than those who have renounced, purity possess they who endure harsh words from the mouth of those who have transgressed limits.
translation: Those who endure harsh words from the mouths of people who transgress all bounds of decency possess a purity greater than even those who have renounced the world.
modern: வரம்பு மீறி நடப்பவர்களுடைய வாயிலிருந்து வரும் துன்பம் தரும் சொற்களைப் பொறுத்துக் கொள்பவர்கள், உலகத்தைத் துறந்தவர்களை விடவும் மேலான தூய்மை உடையவர்கள் ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet compares the spiritual purity of those who practice patience with that of ascetics who have renounced the world. The word 'இறந்தார்' refers to those who have crossed the boundaries of proper conduct and decency. When such people utter 'இன்னாச்சொல்' (painful or abusive words), the act of enduring them ('நோற்கிற்பவர்') requires immense self-control. The poet asserts that this quiet endurance represents a higher level of moral and spiritual purity ('தூய்மை') than the formal renunciation ('துறந்தார்') of worldly life. Thus, patience is elevated to the highest form of spiritual practice.
